title: HB1086 (2018 Regular): Firearms; prohibit public employers from banning employees having permit and training endorsement from carrying on employer's property.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2018/html/HB/1000-1099/HB1086IN.htm)
provenance.note: As-filed text (introduced); no date in text. No vote recorded. Section 1's first sentence is a long single provision; Section 2 reprints the rest of 45-9-101 and sections 97-37-1, 97-37-7 and 45-9-53 are brought forward unchanged.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new section): A public employer of this state or a political subdivision of this state may not adopt or establish a policy prohibiting an employee who has a valid license issued under Section 45-9-101 and a training endorsement as provided by Section 97-37-7 from lawfully carrying a concealed pistol or revolver on any property or in any building under the public employer's control. A sign that is posted by a public employer in accordance with Section 45-9-101 which prohibits the carrying of a concealed pistol or revolver is not effective against any employee of the public employer, provided the employee has a valid license issued under Section 45-9-101 and a training endorsement as provided by Section 97-37-7.
Section 2 (Miss. Code § 45-9-101): However, such sign is not effective against an employee of a public employer who meets the requirements provided in Section 1 of this act.
